svg.text: Simulated devices — the HUD of the binoculars and the laser rangefinder (SD-S1, DESIGN_Simulated_Devices §3.6)
Full colour = SPECIFIED by this mockup · grey dashed + 'unchanged' = CONTEXT drawn from the real station HUD, not specified · the scene behind is illustrative.
specified HUD element (full colour, dark halo — as the station's HudText draws over the 3-D view)
Layout positions are PROPOSALS where the design is silent (it names what the HUD shows, not where) — each panel lists its own.
Frames are 460 × 259 (16:9). The scene is the same in every panel and illustrative; the tank is only there so the reticle has something to rest on.
1 · BINOCULARS — the view bound to the binoculars device
Scope: the two-eyepiece frame, the mil reticle, the zoom step, the device name (D-42,
D-75: replaces the station's overlay). The compass and the unit lines are context.
two-eyepiece frame · mil reticle (5-mil ticks, numbers every 10) · zoom
step 7× of a list · device name
compass strip · unit lines · the 3-D scene
mil scale is true to the lit step's field (7× ⇒ 50°/7 ≈ 7.1°, DeviceOptics — S1d-3 as built;
was today's 10°): 1 mil = 2.08 px; it moves with the zoom.
PROPOSAL: step values 5× / 7× / 10× are illustrative (the type's data); the list sits in the
No range shown: the binoculars carry no laser (the old overlay's RANGE / LMB-designate
2 · RANGEFINDER, idle — laser OFF, nothing measured yet
Scope: the rectangular window, the gapped reticle, mode / power, the laser lamp, the
last range, the menu line. The compass and the unit lines are context.
window + corner brackets · reticle · name · MODE · POWER · LASER lamp
(off) · LAST RANGE '— m' · menu line, cursor on MODE · the button chips
RANGE R · MODE O · MENU P · SELECT ENT (SELECT greyed: the menu is
closed) · SEND Y left of RANGE (greyed: nothing measured, SD-S5b) · the
gold hover frame + hand cursor on RANGE (POINT, SD-S5v)
PROPOSAL: mode names SINGLE / CONTINUOUS and power LOW / HIGH are placeholders
top-right, readout bottom-centre, menu line bottom-right (clear of the unit lines, which
3 · RANGEFINDER, after RANGE on a target — laser ON, 452 m
Scope: the lamp on, the range written, the same layout as panel 2. The spot on the
LASER lamp ON (blinks by frame count) · LAST RANGE '452 m' (gold, the
station's readout colour) · RANGE chip lit while ranging · no cursor (RMB
the red spot (LaserLayer3D, SD-S6) · compass · unit lines
The HUD does NOT draw the spot: it is the 3-D map's laser layer (D-32..D-35, slice SD-S6)
— SD-S1 shows the lamp and the range only.
Judged by scenario dv-range-targets: `hud` text contains the range, `device range` within
4 · RANGEFINDER, menu open — the mode list (dv-menu-and-modes)
Scope: the menu popup (title, the modes, the check on the active one, the cursor row),
the menu line with MODE open. Everything else as panel 2.
popup list · ✓ on the active mode · highlighted cursor row · MODE chip
framed (menu is open) · reticle stays · MENU chip lit, SELECT live, the
The cursor row (CONTINUOUS) is not yet the mode: the state `Mode` changes on select;
PROPOSAL: popup under the status block, left; the reticle and the range stay visible while
5 · RANGEFINDER while the simulation is PAUSED (dv-paused-operation)
Scope: the same HUD still answering in pause: a range measured in pause is shown
marked PREVIEW (R5-10, LS-13). The toolbar's paused state is context.
the HUD still answering in pause: mode (CONTINUOUS, changed by a
press), the lamp, the range, with a PREVIEW tag beside it (a spot written
in pause acts on nothing, R5-10)
the toolbar's run controls (Live, recorded, paused — the indicator + ▶) ·
Measured: no in-view PAUSED banner exists today; the toolbar run indicator is the only
pause cue (a DAR review shows players 'REVIEW — the exercise is paused'). The device HUD
PROPOSAL: the PREVIEW tag's look and place are mine — the design says the HUD shows
the preview spot, not how. Judged on the wall-clock axis (dv-replay-hud).
6 · SWITCHING — the view's bound source (device wheel / cycle)
Scope: the 'VIEW ▸' label of the bound source and the cycle strip shown while
switching. LAYOUT IS A PROPOSAL. Design says: a view is bound to ONE source (D-38
/ D-66); the wheel's key is open (Q-5).
the VIEW ▸ label of the bound source (its glyph in its colour + the device
name, top-right under the lamp) · the cycle strip (eye · binoculars ·
compass · unit lines · the bound device's own HUD (panel 2)
The label is always on while a view shows a device; the strip is drawn only while switching.
Below: the label for each source the strip offers today (more sources — weapon sight,
PROPOSAL (all of it): the strip, the label's place and how long the strip stays are the ui
lane's call; the wheel's key is open (Q-5). The design fixes only: one source per view (D-38 /
D-66), the plain eye is the 'none' source.
